findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring bounds
findings.body: In `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` the check is `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two defects: (1) the grant shortcut occupies characters at index 4 and 5 of the encoded prefix (sessionType=0-1, tokenType=2-3, grantType=4-5), so the bounds must be `substring(4, 6)`, not `(3, 5)`; (2) the condition is inverted - the matcher should fail when the shortcut does NOT equal the expected one, i.e. `!equals(...)`. As written, the two bugs cancel out and every event with a well-formed token id passes regardless of the grant shortcut, so all the new `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` assertions verify nothing about the grant type (and would start failing with false negatives as soon as either half is fixed).

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Any third-party/custom grant type factory compiled against a previous release no longer satisfies the interface and will fail with `AbstractMethodError` (or not compile) once deployed - and because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories and calls `getShortcut()`, the failure happens at server start. Providing a `default` implementation (e.g. deriving a shortcut or returning null and handling it) would keep the SPI backwards compatible.

findings.title: Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking change
findings.body: The `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Subclasses outside this repository (and any code that wrapped a Context, e.g. token-exchange contexts) use it; after this change they can no longer compile/link, and there is no replacement that copies an existing Context. If the copy semantics are no longer needed internally, the constructor should still be kept (deprecated) or an equivalent copy path provided.

findings.title: Context constructor now NPEs on null formParams
findings.body: The constructor now dereferences `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. Previously `formParams` was only stored, so a null value was tolerated by this constructor. Any caller constructing a Context without form parameters now gets a NullPointerException at construction time instead of later (or never). A null-guard (`formParams == null ? null : formParams.getFirst(...)`) would preserve the previous contract.

findings.title: Null check validates grantType twice; rawTokenId is never validated
findings.body: In the constructor, the fourth `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. Consequence: a null `rawTokenId` is accepted and the failure surfaces much later (e.g. a token id literally ending in "null" produced by `encodeTokenId`), and if `grantType` were null the thrown message would be misleading.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType asserts nothing and masks a NullPointerException
findings.body: The test decodes "ofrtac:5678" and only catches `RuntimeException`. Because the test factory is never `postInit`-ed, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory` is null, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` throws a NullPointerException rather than the intended `IllegalArgumentException`. The test therefore passes for the wrong reason and does not verify the documented error behaviour; it also hides that the production lookup path dereferences `sessionFactory` unconditionally. Catch/assert `IllegalArgumentException` explicitly (and initialize `sessionFactory`).

findings.title: Decoding throws IllegalArgumentException for any token id containing ':' in an unexpected format
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` treats any id containing ':' as encoded and then throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the prefix is not exactly 6 characters or if a shortcut is unknown. Token ids produced by a different/older encoder, by a custom `TokenContextEncoderProvider`, or by a federated/externally issued token could legitimately contain ':' and would cause an unhandled runtime exception (HTTP 500) in whatever endpoint decodes the id, instead of degrading to an UNKNOWN context like the no-colon case does. Also the message "Expected length of 6" refers to the prefix, not the token id that is printed, which is confusing.

findings.title: Lazy shortcut cache refresh can NPE and bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation
findings.body: `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` lazily insert into the `ConcurrentHashMap`s for grant types discovered after `postInit`. If a (custom) `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns null, `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantType)` throws NullPointerException; the same happens in `postInit`, failing server startup with an opaque error instead of a message naming the offending factory. In addition, the duplicate-shortcut consistency check performed in `postInit` is not applied on these lazy inserts, so a newly deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites an existing mapping, making decoded grant types wrong.

findings.title: Session type derived from clientSession.getUserSession() instead of the user session already available
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` resolves the user session via `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` and immediately dereferences it. `TokenManager.initToken`, the only caller, already has a non-null `userSession` parameter it uses for exactly the same persistence-state check. For client session contexts whose client session is not (yet) attached to a user session this call yields a NullPointerException during access token creation. Passing/using the known `userSession` removes the risk and the redundant lookup.

findings.title: Externally visible jti format change without upgrade documentation
findings.body: Access token `jti` values change from a bare UUID to `<6-char prefix>:<uuid>` (and the same value is reported in the `token_id` event detail). Relying parties, log pipelines and tests that assume `jti` is a UUID (or validate its length/charset) will break. The PR contains no upgrading-guide/release-note entry describing this behaviour change or the new `tokenContextEncoder` SPI.
